newsitem.title: USA: Levi Strauss employee records missing.
newsitem.headline: Levi Strauss employee records missing.

text.p: A computer hard drive containing personal and financial information about employees of jeans giant Levi Strauss & Co. is missing from company headquarters, a spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The San Francisco-based company did not know what happened to the drive but said in a statement it was "operating under the assumption that the drive has been stolen."
The drive's disappearance was discovered during a routine inspection last week and Levi Strauss said it had the information stored on backup.
News reports said the drive contained information on more than 20,000 current and retired Levi Strauss workers in the United States, but company spokeswoman Linda Butler declined to give any number.
The information could conceivably be used for credit or bank fraud but Levi Strauss said it did not think this was likely.
"Most of the information is general in nature and is written in a complicated computer language that would be difficult to decode," a company statement said.
The San Francisco Police Department was helping to investigate the disappearance of the drive, it said.

The information contained on the drive included employees' names, addresses, dates of birth and social security numbers, the statement said. The drive also contained the bank account numbers of some retirees.
Privately owned Levi Strauss said it had told affected employees about the missing drive and had recommended that they notify their banks and contact a credit reporting agency to monitor their files.
Butler said it was possible that someone could have stolen the drive for its value as a computer component rather than for the data stored on it.
